conceptZh: 菜：草字頭加「采」，採來吃的青菜；披風英雄和一棵愛模仿的小青菜一起把葉子排成字。
object: a caped action-figure hero with a far-too-long crimson cape, and a tiny bok choy sprout with a face that copies him
morph: hero and the mimicking sprout swing leafy blades one beat apart until the blades land as the top grass radical and the lower strokes of 菜
creativeAngle: 披風英雄的披風長三號，老是蓋住自己的頭；一棵小青菜學他每個動作，慢一拍，結果兩邊揮出的葉片剛好落成字的筆畫。
promptEn: An 8-second bright, clean toy-animation clip on a solid pale butter-yellow backdrop, no props beyond those named. Cast: a chunky caped action-figure hero with a crimson cape three sizes too long that keeps flopping over his own head, plus one tiny bok choy sprout with a round face that mimics him one beat late. The only text on screen is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 菜, drawn in saturated leaf-green strokes with a slightly darker edge, finishing centered, uncropped, about 70 percent of frame height with margins. 0.0-1.5s: the hero slides in on one foot and strikes a grand sword-swing pose holding a long leaf blade; the cape flops over his face and he peeks out. The first narrated 菜 lands as the blade swishes and leaves a green horizontal stroke hanging in the air. 1.5-3.5s: the bok choy sprout pops up from a little clay pot at his feet and copies the swing a beat late, whacking the hero's boot; both blades flick and the two top strokes of the grass radical settle together. The second narrated 菜 lands exactly as the radical clicks in. 3.5-5.0s: the hero spins to shake off the cape, the sprout spins too, one beat behind, and tangles itself in the cape's tail; their wobbly swings throw green leaf strokes down in a neat row and the lower part of the glyph fills in. As the word is spoken the sprout hops into a small wooden crate and a fresh pile of glossy green vegetables pops up beside it. 5.0-8.0s: the finished glyph is perfectly still and fully readable for the last 3 seconds while the hero, off to one side, tries a proud pose, the cape flops over his head again, and the sprout copies with a tiny bow. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin, reading exactly these syllables with clear tones and no erhua: 菜、菜、青菜 (ㄘㄞˋ、ㄘㄞˋ、ㄑㄧㄥ ㄘㄞˋ). Say the character twice with a short pause, then the word once, then stop. The word is audio only. No background music, no extra speech, no subtitles, labels, watermarks or flashing effects; all characters are stylized toys or cartoon creatures, with no real people.

conceptZh: 披風英雄想摘一顆比他還大的巨無霸高麗菜，第一次衝鋒被披風蓋住頭撞到布忍者的煙霧彈，第二次用力後仰衝刺「碰」一聲撞上大菜，震落的兩株嫩芽、三片葉尖和粗菜梗掉下來排成「菜」字。
object: a giant glossy green cabbage, bigger than the hero, sitting on the right side of the frame like a boulder
morph: the crash shakes three kinds of pieces loose: two leafy sprouts fall as the grass radical 艹 on top, three small leaf tips drop as the claw 爫 in the middle, and the cabbage's thick stalk lands as 木 at the bottom, stacking into 菜 while the cabbage rolls off-frame
creativeAngle: 上一版是模仿揮劍的安靜排字，這一版改成完整的「衝鋒撞擊」：目標是巨大高麗菜，呼應「菜」的草字頭和「采＝採摘」的意思；第一次失敗靠披風蓋頭加布忍者的煙霧彈製造更大的笑點，第二次大撞擊震落的三種碎片剛好對應艹、爫、木三層結構，字由撞擊本身堆出來，而不是慢慢變形。
promptEn:
An 8-second bright, clean toy-animation clip on a solid pale mint-cream backdrop with a soft flat floor, nothing busy behind. Cast: a chunky caped action-figure hero with a crimson cape three sizes too long that keeps flopping over his own head, and one tiny felt ninja who thinks he is invisible. Prop: a giant glossy green cabbage, bigger than the hero, sitting at the right edge like a boulder. The only text on screen is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 菜, drawn in saturated leaf-green strokes with a darker green edge, finishing centered, uncropped, about 70 percent of frame height with even margins.

0.0-1.5s: the hero stands at the far left, spots the giant cabbage, points at it with both arms and rubs his tummy. He digs both boots into the floor and leans way back in a huge wind-up. The first spoken 菜 lands on the point.

1.5-3.0s: first charge. Two steps in, the cape flops over his head and he sprints blind in a wobbly curve, straight into the felt ninja, who is standing in plain view beside the cabbage holding one leaf in front of his face as camouflage. The ninja's smoke bomb pops early in a soft puff; the hero bounces backward out of the cloud to his starting spot, coughs once, and shakes the cape off his face.

3.0-4.5s: he leans back even farther, cape pinned under one arm this time, freezes for a beat of anticipation, then charges across the frame at full speed and hits the cabbage with a big squashy BONK. He squashes flat against it, the cabbage wobbles and bounces, and pieces fly loose: two leafy sprouts, three small leaf tips and the thick pale stalk. The cabbage rolls off the right edge.

4.5-5.5s: the pieces drop into place as the glyph 菜: the two sprouts settle on top as the grass radical 艹, the three leaf tips land below as the claw 爫, and the thick stalk stands at the bottom as 木. The second spoken 菜 lands exactly as the last stroke clicks in.

5.5-8.0s: the finished glyph is perfectly still, centered and fully readable for the final hold. Off to the lower left, the flattened hero peels himself up, wobbles with a dizzy grin and gives a thumbs-up. As the word is spoken, the ninja pops out of his smoke on the lower right proudly holding up a fresh bunch of glossy green leafy vegetables. The hero strikes a victory pose, and the cape flops over his head one more time. Nobody touches the strokes.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin, reading exactly these syllables with clear tones and no erhua: 菜、菜、青菜 (ㄘㄞˋ、ㄘㄞˋ、ㄑㄧㄥ ㄘㄞˋ). Say the character twice with a short pause between, then the word once, then stop. The word is audio only. Soft cartoon bonk and puff sounds, no background music, no extra speech, no subtitles, labels, watermarks or flashing effects; all characters are stylized toys, with no real people.
